newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - April 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - April 25.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
HEART RISK OF HAY FEVER PILLS

The Department of Health has revealed that 14 people have died since 1982 from cardiac ailments related to taking hay fever medication containing the drug Terfenadine. The government has not issued an immediate ban on the products, but has started a 3 month consultation period, after which they drugs could be made prescription only.

A survey by Meis has revealed that bonus schemes at top British companies pay directors for below-par performance. Typically, directors of FT-SE 100 companies would start to cash in if their performance was only 55th out of 100.

David Abell, the controversial former Suter chairman, has effectively won 38.9 percent control of retail supplier Thomas Jourdan, which will make it much harder for Jourdan to fend off Abell's demands for the resignation of the company's chairman and chief executive Keith Whitten.
BANKS WIN 1.5BN STG RUSSIAN GAS DEAL

Goldman Sachs and ABN Amro have pulled off a deal to advise Russian gas utility RAO Gazprom over its plans to raise $2.5 billion (1.5 billion stg) in the international debt markets this year. Gazprom plans a series of convertible straight Eurobond issues, plus a syndicated loan programme.
